targetText:
The rate of surplus-value is therefore an exact expression for
the degree of exploitation of labour-power by capital, or of the labourer
by the capitalist. [7]
explanation: The rate of surplus value (s / v) measures the degree of exploitation: the ratio of unpaid surplus labor time to paid necessary labor time.

targetText: surplus-value bears the same ratio to variable capital, that surplus-labour does to necessary labour, or in other words, the rate of surplus-value, s/v = (surplus labour)/(necessary labour). Both ratios, s/v and (surplus labour)/(necessary labour), express the same thing in different ways; in the one case by reference to materialised, incorporated labour, in the other by reference to living, fluent labour.
summary: The rate of surplus-value formula: the ratio of surplus-labour to necessary labour expressed in materialised and living form.
explanation: Marx demonstrates that s/v is identical to the ratio of surplus labour-time to necessary labour-time. Whether measured in monetary value or in living hours worked, this fraction reveals the precise proportion of unpaid labour extracted from the working class.
context: Part III, Chapter 9: The Rate of Surplus-Value
